proposals.evidence: DEDR3538 gives Tamil tōkai tail, Malayalam tōka, Kannada tōke, Gondi tōkār/tōkor/tōkar/tōka and Konda tōka tail. Selected simple survey tok-/tōk- responses match this family, retaining gemination and lect-specific final vowels. Gondi teke and other more divergent responses remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR183 explicitly gives Tamil ammā, Malayalam amma, Kannada amma/ama, Telugu amma and numerous other mother/honorific uses. The selected survey amma/ammā mother responses belong to this nursery-word family. The Sanskrit ambā comparison and independent nursery-word formation limit the historical claim; no immediate borrowing direction is asserted, and lects using amme for father remain separate. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3656 explicitly gives Tamil nāḷai/nāḷaikku, Malayalam nāḷa, Kannada nāḷe, Kodagu nāḷe/nāḷēkï, Gondi nāṛ(i) and Kurux nelā tomorrow. Selected survey forms preserve the day-stem temporal/locative endings, including nāḷɛykɨ and regional vowel/lateral variants; these are ordinary inflected temporal forms. Opaque contractions and multiword temporal responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2646 gives Kannada cikki/cikke star, Gadaba sukka and Gondi sukkum/huko/hukka/ukkum/ukka/ukam star. Selected cukk-/sukk-/ukk- survey nouns preserve documented sibilant weakening, stem-final vowels and ordinary plural endings. DEDR explicitly marks Tamil cukkai as a Telugu loan; no Tamil response is included in this inherited-family proposal. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
